elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall not occur more than once in any Calendar Year". Calendar Year is defined as the Jan 1–Dec 31 period, so two audits could still fall in December and the following January, i.e. within a single rolling 12-month period. A "once in any twelve (12)-month period" formulation would be needed for the preferred element.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a) sets notice at "at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" — the fallback figure, not the 30 days required at the preferred level.
No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in 9.9(a)-(d); the drafter expressly declines to press this point.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) (unchanged): "permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: 9.9(d) (unchanged): the Parties "shall cause the auditor to enter into a reasonably acceptable confidentiality agreement with the audited Party obligating such auditor to retain all such financial information in confidence"; 9.9(b) also bars disclosure of the audited Party's Confidential Information beyond verification needs.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site/remote-review preference is stated in 9.9; the clause is silent on audit location.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c) shifts cost only where the underpayment "was more than ten percent (10%)" — the fallback threshold, above the 5% preferred trigger.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: 9.9(a) confines the auditor to "the books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8" and 9.9(b) limits the report, but there is no express prohibition on access to Customer systems and no statement that records are produced rather than accessed in situ; scope limitation implies but does not operatively state the no-system-access element.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall not occur more than once in any Calendar Year", with the open-ended "unless for cause" carve-out deleted, so the annual cap is a hard ceiling with a definite number replacing the [***] placeholder.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "but in any event at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice" replaces the [***] placeholder with an operative 15-day floor.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c): "The auditing Party shall bear the full cost of such audit unless such audit reveals an underpayment ... more than ten percent (10%) of the amount set forth in such report" — cost sits with the auditing (Vendor) side unless the 10% trigger is exceeded.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete on the operative face of the rendered clause: a hard once-per-Calendar-Year cap, a 15-day prior notice floor, and Vendor-side cost bearing unless underpayment exceeds 10%. Each replaced a redacted [***] placeholder that left the limit unenforceable, so the original clause did fail the fallback on material terms and the 'deviation' classification is correct.

Deletion of the "unless for cause" carve-out is necessary rather than cosmetic: without it the annual cap is not a ceiling at all, so it is properly within the frequency element and does not break minimality.

Minimality otherwise holds — no survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra requirements were added, and the favourable existing terms (independent auditor of international prominence, auditor confidentiality agreement, report-scope limits, books-and-records-only scope, interest and dispute mechanics) are untouched. The single added word "written" in the notice sentence is a de minimis modifier that tracks the rule's own notice element; it is noted but not treated as a minimality failure.

Intent is preserved: the clause remains mutual as originally drafted (Section 6.9 running the other way is left alone), no cross-reference is orphaned, and the remaining [***] placeholders (record look-back period in 9.9(a) and payment window in 9.9(b)) are pre-existing redactions the edit did not create or contradict.

Preferred level is not reached and the rationale correctly does not claim it. If the drafter wants to push to preferred, the operative repairs are: change "once in any Calendar Year" to "once in any twelve (12)-month period" (a Calendar Year cap permits back-to-back December/January audits), raise notice to "thirty (30) days", lower the cost-shift trigger in 9.9(c) to "five percent (5%)", add "during the audited Party's normal business hours" and an "off-site where reasonably possible" preference, and add an express statement that the auditor shall have no direct access to the audited Party's systems or networks.
